messages.author: 90b5ae7e2259370d
messages.subject: Computing log likelihood in generated quantities block
parts:
Hi all,

I'm trying to compute log likelihood for my model (reinforcement learning model) to compute the WAIC for model comparison. Everything is working, but I'm not sure whether there would be a more economical way to code it as at the moment I seem to have to repeat most of my model in the 'generated quantities' block - I'm not sure whether there is a way around this? This is a slight problem because it might make this quite prone to errors if I'm changing something in the model block, but then forget to change it in the generated quantities block without it producing any errors etc.

Many thanks
Jacquie

data{
  int nsub;
  int mtr;           // maximal number of trials per person (=240)
  int Dec[nsub,mtr]; // real choices
  real RMagO[nsub,mtr];
  real Prob[nsub,mtr];
  int Symbs[nsub,mtr];   // 1 or 2 are normal symbols, 3 and 4 should be ignored for learning
}

parameters{
  // Group level
  real<lower=0,upper=1>  mu_alpha;
  real<lower=0,upper=10> mu_beta;
  real<lower=0,upper=1>  mu_relre;    // relative weight of learnt reward to effort

  // Group level standard deviation
  real<lower=0> sd_alpha;
  real<lower=0> sd_beta;
  real<lower=0> sd_relre;

  // Individual-level parameters (will be drawn from group distributions
  real<lower=0,upper=1>  alpha[nsub]; 
  real<lower=0,upper=10> beta[nsub];
  real<lower=0,upper=1>  relre[nsub]; 
}


model{
  // Variables that will be computed in the model
  real RMagP[nsub,mtr,2];
  real EMagP[nsub,mtr,2];
  real Util[nsub,mtr,2];    // Utility     
  real DecP[nsub,mtr];      // Predicted choice (Utility transformed by softmax)

  real log_lik[nsub,mtr]; 


  // Priors - group
  mu_alpha ~ uniform(0,1);
  mu_beta  ~ uniform(0,10);
  mu_relre ~ uniform(0,1);

  sd_alpha ~ uniform(0,1.5); // value from pvl_d.stan model
  sd_beta  ~ uniform(0,1.5);
  sd_relre ~ uniform(0,1.5);

  // Single sub drawn from normal distr.
  for (s in 1:nsub){
    alpha[s] ~ normal(mu_alpha,sd_alpha);
    beta[s]  ~ normal(mu_beta,sd_beta);
    relre[s] ~ normal(mu_relre,sd_relre);
  }
  // Compute learning
  for (s in 1:nsub){
    for (t in 1:mtr){
      if (t==1 || t==121){  // detect first trial of set
RMagP[s,t+1,:]  <- RMagO[s,t,:];
      }
      else if (Dec[s,t]!=1000 && t!=120 && t!=240) { // actual learning
for (o in 1:2){
  if (Symbs[s,t,o]<3){
    RMagP[s,t+1,o] <- RMagP[s,t,o] + alpha[s]*(RMagO[s,t,o]-RMagP[s,t,o]);
          }
  else {
    RMagP[s,t+1,o] <- RMagP[s,t,o];
  }
}
      }
    }
  }

  // Compute utility and assign decisions (only on normal trials
  for (s in 1:nsub){
    for (t in 1:mtr){
      if (Dec[s,t]!=1000 && Symbs[s,t,1]<3 && Symbs[s,t,2]<3&& t!=1 &&t!=121){
for (o in 1:2){
  Util[s,t,o] <- relre[s]*RMagP[s,t,o] + Prob[s,t,o];
}
DecP[s,t] <- 1.0/(1.0+exp(beta[s]*(Util[s,t,2]-Util[s,t,1])));
        Dec[s,t] ~ bernoulli(DecP[s,t]);
      }
    }
  }
}

generated quantities{
  real RMagP[nsub,mtr,2];
  real Util[nsub,mtr,2];    // Utility     
  real DecP[nsub,mtr];      // Predicted choice (Utility transformed by softmax)
  real log_lik[nsub,mtr];


  // Compute learning
  for (s in 1:nsub){
    for (t in 1:mtr){
      if (t==1 || t==121){  // detect first trial of set
   RMagP[s,t+1,:]  <- RMagO[s,t,:];
      }
      else if (Dec[s,t]!=1000 && t!=120 && t!=240) { // actual learning
   for (o in 1:2){
     if (Symbs[s,t,o]<3){
       RMagP[s,t+1,o] <- RMagP[s,t,o] + alpha[s]*(RMagO[s,t,o]-RMagP[s,t,o]);
          }
     else {
       RMagP[s,t+1,o] <- RMagP[s,t,o];
     }
   }
      }
    }
  }

  // Compute utility and assign decisions (only on normal trials
  for (s in 1:nsub){
    for (t in 1:mtr){
      if (Dec[s,t]!=1000 && Symbs[s,t,1]<3 && Symbs[s,t,2]<3&& t!=1 &&t!=121){
   for (o in 1:2){
     Util[s,t,o] <- relre[s]*RMagP[s,t,o] + Prob[s,t,o];
   }
   DecP[s,t] <- 1.0/(1.0+exp(beta[s]*(Util[s,t,2]-Util[s,t,1])));
log_lik[s,t] <- bernoulli_log(Dec[s,t],DecP[s,t])
      }

    }
  }
}

messages.author: fc5d3270037d7478
messages.subject: Re: Computing log likelihood in generated quantities block
parts:
Hi Jacquie, 

I suggest creating a user-defined function in the functions block that computes the log-likelihood. Then you can use it in the model block and generated quantities. The "User Defined Functions" section of manual goes through how to do this, but if you run into any trouble let us know. 

Jonah

messages.author: da33143a8db60ce8
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Computing log likelihood in generated quantities block
parts:
Yes, but this doesn’t always make sense because it can give up the efficiency that would be gained by vectorization. In my examples I found it made more sense to just use near-duplicate code, ugly as that is, with vectorized computation in the model block and point-by-point computation in the generated quantities block. We discuss this in our paper.
A

      if (Dec[s,t]!=1000 && Symbs[s,t,1]<3 && Symbs[s,t,2]<3&& t!=1 &&t!=121){
   for (o in 1:2){
     Util[s,t,o] <- relre[s]*RMagP[s,t,o] + Prob[s,t,o];
   }
   DecP[s,t] <- 1.0/(1.0+exp(beta[s]*(Util[s,t,2]-Util[s,t,1])));
log_lik[s,t] <- bernoulli_log(Dec[s,t],DecP[s,t])
      }

    }
  }
}

On Thursday, February 4, 2016, Jacqueline Scholl <jacquie...@gmail.com> wrote:
actually, using the function block as you advised solves this - only the 'returned' variable from the function is stored. thank you again for the tip!

Glad that's working for you. In general, you can also create local blocks using { } inside of generated quantities if you only want to store a subset of quantities you define. For example 

generated quantities {
  real x;
  x <- 1.5;
 {
  real y;
  y <- 0.5;
  x <- x + y;
 }
} 

will only save x (with a value of 2) and y will be dropped since it's defined in a local block. 

Hope that helps,

Jonah
